Why packages? Package structure and states

DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R/, man/

Documentation with roxygen2 and tests with testthat

Building a package from scratch (live, with base R)

Checking, GitHub, and CRAN

::: notes - Adapted from the STAR-DS and SCoRT short courses (R package / CRAN submission). Main reference: Wickham and Bryan, *R Packages*, 2nd ed., . - Running example: package the S3 `knnreg` class from the OOP lecture into a package `knnreg`. ::: ## R Packages: The Fundamental Unit In R, the **fundamental unit of shareable code** is the **package**. A package bundles together - **code** (functions, classes, methods), - **data**, - **documentation** (help pages, vignettes), - **tests**, all in one place, easy to share, install, and cite. ::: question You already use packages: `install.packages("boot")`, `library(boot)`, `help(package = "boot")`. What would it take to make **your** HW functions installable like that? ::: ## Why Write a Package? - To **share** your code (classmates, collaborators, your future self) - To make your code easy to **install, use, and learn** - To save time with **conventions**: R CMD check finds problems you didn't know you had - Research software (e.g. an estimator from a paper) is expected to be a package - Course connection: the `knnreg` class, a Monte Carlo integrator, a bootstrap function ... all are package-sized ## Package Structure ```text knnreg/ ├── DESCRIPTION # package metadata ├── NAMESPACE # exported functions & imports ├── R/ # your R functions ├── man/ # documentation (.Rd), generated by roxygen2 ├── tests/ # unit tests with testthat ├── data/ # data sets (.rda) ├── src/ # C/C++ code (Rcpp, Ch 15) ├── vignettes/ # long-form documentation (Rmd/qmd) └── inst/ # installed as-is (e.g. inst/app/ for a Shiny app, extdata/) ``` ::: tip Only `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE`, and `R/` are required; add the others as needed. ::: ## Package States - **Source:** the editable folder. - **Bundled:** a `.tar.gz` built from source (`R CMD build`); portable, not yet usable. - **Binary:** precompiled for one OS (`.zip` on Windows, `.tgz` on macOS). - **Installed:** unpacked into a library folder (`R CMD INSTALL`, `install.packages()`). - **In-memory:** loaded into a session (`library()`, or `devtools::load_all()` during development). ![](images/rpkg/install-load.png){width="45%" fig-align="center"} ## System Setup ```{.r} install.packages(c("devtools", "usethis", "roxygen2", "testthat", "knitr", "rmarkdown")) devtools::has_devel() # do you have a working build toolchain? ``` - **Windows:** install [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) (matching your R version) for packages with compiled code. - **macOS:** `xcode-select --install`. - `usethis` creates files and folders; `devtools` builds, documents, tests, and checks; `roxygen2` writes help pages and the NAMESPACE. ## Choosing a Name and Creating the Package A valid name contains only letters, numbers, and periods, starts with a letter, and does not end with a period. Check availability: `available::available("knnreg")`. ```{.r} usethis::create_package("~/R/knnreg") # opens a new RStudio/Positron project usethis::use_mit_license() usethis::use_r("knnreg") # creates R/knnreg.R usethis::use_testthat() usethis::use_test("knnreg") # creates tests/testthat/test-knnreg.R usethis::use_data(mydata) # saves data/mydata.rda usethis::use_git(); usethis::use_github() ``` ![](images/rpkg/create_pkg.png){width="45%" fig-align="center"} ## The DESCRIPTION File ```{.yaml} Package: knnreg Title: k-Nearest-Neighbor Regression with S3 Methods Version: 0.1.0 Authors@R: person("First", "Last", email = "first.last@marquette.edu", role = c("aut", "cre")) Description: Fits k-nearest-neighbor regression models, with print, predict, and cross-validation methods. Written for MATH 4750 Computational Statistics. License: MIT + file LICENSE Encoding: UTF-8 Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) RoxygenNote: 7.3.2 Imports: stats Suggests: testthat (>= 3.0.0), shiny Config/testthat/edition: 3 ``` - **Imports:** needed for your package to work (installed automatically). **Suggests:** optional (tests, vignettes, apps). Never call `library()` inside package code; use `pkg::fun()` or `@importFrom`. ## The NAMESPACE File ```text # Generated by roxygen2: do not edit by hand S3method(predict,knnreg) S3method(print,knnreg) export(cv_error) export(knnreg) importFrom(stats,sd) ``` - `export()`: functions users can call. Everything else is internal (`knnreg:::helper`). - `S3method()`: registers methods for generics. - `importFrom()`: functions you use from other packages. - Generated from roxygen tags by `devtools::document()`. ## Documenting with roxygen2 ```{.r} #' Fit a k-nearest-neighbor regression #' #' @param x A numeric matrix or data frame of predictors. #' @param y A numeric response vector. #' @param k Number of neighbors. #' @return An object of class `knnreg`. #' @examples #' fit <- knnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = 5) #' predict(fit, data.frame(wt = 3, qsec = 18)) #' @export knnreg <- function(x, y, k = 5) { validate_knnreg(new_knnreg(as.matrix(x), as.numeric(y), as.integer(k))) } #' @export predict.knnreg <- function(object, newdata = object$x, k = object$k, ...) { ... } ``` `devtools::document()` turns these comments into `man/knnreg.Rd` and the NAMESPACE. ## Testing with testthat ```{.r} # tests/testthat/test-knnreg.R test_that("k = n predicts the mean", { fit <- knnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = nrow(mtcars)) expect_equal(predict(fit, data.frame(wt = 3, qsec = 18)), mean(mtcars$mpg)) }) test_that("invalid k is an error", { expect_error(knnreg(mtcars[, 1:2], mtcars$mpg, k = 0), "between 1 and n") }) ``` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(testthat) test_that("the sample mean is the k = n k-NN fit", { y <- c(3, 1, 4, 1, 5) expect_equal(mean(y[order(abs(1:5 - 2))[1:5]]), mean(y)) }) ``` ::: ## The Development Loop ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/12-rpkg/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: - `devtools::load_all()` simulates installing and attaching: fast iteration without reinstalling. - `devtools::check()` runs **R CMD check**: the gold standard. ![](images/rpkg/check.png){width="40%" fig-align="center"} # Build a Package from Scratch (Live) ## Step 1: Create the Source Folder with Base R No helper packages needed: a package is just files. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "knnreg") unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE); dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE) writeLines(c( "Package: knnreg", "Title: k-Nearest-Neighbor Regression with S3 Methods", "Version: 0.1.0", "Authors@R: person('MATH', 'Student', email = 'student@marquette.edu', role = c('aut', 'cre'))", "Description: Fits k-nearest-neighbor regression models with print and predict methods.", "License: MIT + file LICENSE", "Encoding: UTF-8", "Imports: stats"), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")) writeLines(c("YEAR: 2027", "COPYRIGHT HOLDER: knnreg authors"), file.path(pkg, "LICENSE")) writeLines(c("export(knnreg)", "S3method(print,knnreg)", "S3method(predict,knnreg)", "importFrom(stats,sd)"), file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE")) ``` ::: ## Step 2: Add the Code ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} code <- ' knnreg <- function(x, y, k = 5) { x <- as.matrix(x); y <- as.numeric(y); k <- as.integer(k) if (nrow(x) != length(y)) stop("`x` and `y` must have the same number of observations") if (k < 1 || k > nrow(x)) stop("`k` must be between 1 and n") structure(list(x = x, y = y, k = k, center = colMeans(x), scale = apply(x, 2, sd)), class = "knnreg") } print.knnreg <- function(x, ...) { cat("k-NN regression with k =", x$k, "on", nrow(x$x), "observations\\n"); invisible(x) } predict.knnreg <- function(object, newdata = object$x, k = object$k, ...) { tr <- scale(object$x, object$center, object$scale) te <- scale(as.matrix(newdata), object$center, object$scale) apply(te, 1, function(x0) mean(object$y[order(colSums((t(tr) - x0)^2))[1:k]])) }' writeLines(code, file.path(pkg, "R", "knnreg.R")) list.files(pkg, recursive = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "DESCRIPTION" "LICENSE" "NAMESPACE" "R/knnreg.R" ``` ::: ::: ## Step 3: Build, Install, and Use ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} lib <- file.path(tempdir(), "lib"); dir.create(lib, showWarnings = FALSE) owd <- setwd(tempdir()) out <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), c("CMD", "build", "--no-manual", "knnreg"), stdout = TRUE) tail(out, 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "* checking for empty or unneeded directories" [2] "* building 'knnreg_0.1.0.tar.gz'" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} tarball <- list.files(pattern = "^knnreg_.*tar.gz$") install.packages(tarball, lib = lib, repos = NULL, type = "source", quiet = TRUE) setwd(owd) library(knnreg, lib.loc = lib) fit <- knnreg(mtcars[, c("wt", "qsec")], mtcars$mpg, k = 5) fit ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` k-NN regression with k = 5 on 32 observations ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} predict(fit, data.frame(wt = c(2, 3.5), qsec = c(20, 17))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 27.58 17.18 ``` ::: ::: ::: notes - In practice use devtools::build() and devtools::install(); here we show that only base R is needed. - Note the bundled tarball name: knnreg_0.1.0.tar.gz. ::: ## Data, Compiled Code, and Apps in a Package - **Data:** `usethis::use_data(df)` $\rightarrow$ `data/df.rda`; document it in `R/data.R` with `@format` and `@source`. - **C++ (Ch 15):** `usethis::use_rcpp()`; put code in `src/`; `// [[Rcpp::export]]`; `LinkingTo: Rcpp` in DESCRIPTION. - **Shiny app:** put it in `inst/app/app.R` and export a launcher: ```{.r} #' Launch the k-NN explorer #' @export run_explorer <- function() { app_dir <- system.file("app", package = "knnreg") shiny::runApp(app_dir, display.mode = "normal") } ``` ## Sharing: GitHub and CRAN :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **GitHub** ```{.r} usethis::use_git() usethis::use_github() usethis::use_readme_rmd() usethis::use_github_action("check-standard") # users install with remotes::install_github("user/knnreg") ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **CRAN checklist** - `R CMD check --as-cran`: 0 ERRORs, 0 WARNINGs, minimal NOTEs - All exported functions documented, examples run in < 5 s - Valid license, plain-text Title/Description - `rhub::rhub_check()` on Windows/macOS/Linux - `devtools::release()` (or the web form) ::: :::: ![](images/rpkg/Cran_Rfssa.png){width="38%" fig-align="center"} ## After Submission - Automated confirmation e-mail; a CRAN maintainer reviews within days. - They may accept, request fixes, or reject with reasons. Respond politely and resubmit with a bumped version (1.0.0 $\rightarrow$ 1.0.1) and `cran-comments.md`. - Keep a `NEWS.md`; tag releases on GitHub. ## Summary ::: instructions - A package = DESCRIPTION + NAMESPACE + R/ (+ man/, tests/, data/, src/, inst/, vignettes/). - `usethis` creates; `roxygen2` documents; `testthat` tests; `devtools` loads, builds, and checks. - The loop: edit $\rightarrow$ `load_all()` $\rightarrow$ `document()` $\rightarrow$ `test()` $\rightarrow$ `check()`. - Share via GitHub; submit to CRAN when `check()` is clean. ::: ::: your-turn **Final-project tip:** turn your project code into a small package with at least two exported, documented functions, one S3 class with a `print` method, and three unit tests. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
